claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has an as-processed hierarchical heterostructure exhibiting multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Phase interfaces mediate the macroscopic mechanical response of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Mesoscale chemical fluctuations mediate the macroscopic mechanical response of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Grain-scale heterogeneities mediate the macroscopic mechanical response of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Physics-based constraints restrict the machine-learning solution space to physically realistic regimes.
Physics-informed modeling enables the model to identify and emphasize the microstructural information critical to mechanical behavior.
The reduced-order model can bypass costly full-scale simulations.
The proposed model will improve the predictive accuracy of Young's modulus by roughly 20–30% relative to the stated baseline methods.
The proposed model will improve the predictive accuracy of yield strength by roughly 20–30% relative to the stated baseline methods.
The proposed model will improve the predictive accuracy of fracture toughness by roughly 20–30% relative to the stated baseline methods.

The proposed model will provide a several-fold to approximately one-order-of-magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to conventional CALPHAD, first-principles, or black-box machine-learning approaches.
The model may become less reliable at temperatures outside its calibration range.
The model may become less reliable at strain rates outside its calibration range.
The model may become less reliable when the material's hierarchical heterostructure differs substantially from structures represented in the training data.
High-resolution imaging and statistical analysis can provide representative descriptors of the relevant hierarchical heterostructure and chemical fluctuations.
